Tested on Fedora 42 with KDE Plasma on Wayland, I don't seem to reproduce the issue.
GPU: AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV PHOENIX)

Sometimes you have to restart Godot and load the save file again to crash, it is really random.
I have a big project right now where it always crashes. Maybe I can upload a minified version of it later

I tried a few more times but still no crash for me. It might be driver specific, as you're on Nvidia and I'm on AMD.

If you're able to compile Godot from source, compiling with `scons dev_build=yes` should include debug symbols and may provide more information about where the crash happens.

I've noticed the same thing happening to me... running Gnome with Wayland on Fedora 42, AMD drivers.

I also believe it is caused by the use of occlusion culling, given I can prevent any crashing by simply disabling the occlusion culling in Godot's project settings. It seems very random; maybe one in three times that I start Godot with occlusion culling enabled will it crash after just a couple frames. Hopefully we can find a solution soon!

Have noticed the same issue on my hardware after recently switching over to linux
I am running Nobara Linux 42 using Wayland
CPU: 16 × AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor
RAM: 30,3 GiB of RAM
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT

Removing the occluder resource from the occluderinstance3d stops the game from crashing.
For me the editor does not crash, but the game does whenever I instantiate the scene containing the occluderinstance3d without any sort of error message. It also does not ALWAYS happen. Sometimes it just ... doesnt crash ... 
It crashes in 15 out of 20 tests

This issue still persists. Didn't happen on versions prior to 4.4. Here's my specs and what I have encountered in my attempts to get around this.
CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core
GPU: Nvidia RTX 5090
Distro: Arch Linux
Running KDE Wayland

- The crash only happens in 3D view where there is a visible OccluderInstance3D with an occlusion shape enabled that must have at least one polygon on it.
- An empty occluder array or empty PolygonOccluder doesn't cause crash.
- The OccluderInstance3D has to be marked visible and it must not be child of another object that has been marked invisible, otherwise there is no crash.
- It doesn't matter if the OccluderInstance3D is in front of the camera or not. It also doesn't matter if it is too small to even fill one pixel, a polygon with all of its vertices in the exact same coordinates still crashes the editor.

Sometimes I have gotten lucky and the editor doesn't crash. Then I can continue editing the scene and enable hundreds of OccluderInstances without issues. I am not sure if having multiple occluder instances enabled at the start increases the chance of crash, but at least once one of them is enabled without issue, the rest will work too.

When launching the game in editor with OccluderInstances in the scene, it often crashes with signal 11. I get following error in terminal repeatedly when this happens:

```
ERROR: Caller thread can't call this function in this node (/root). Use call_deferred() or call_thread_group() instead.
   at: propagate_notification (scene/main/node.cpp:2552)
```

I hope this helps.

Hello

I am also experiencing this issue on two computers. The minimal reproduction in the OP does trigger the crash for me.

I've compiled a dev build of Godot 4.5.1 for testing. I've tried running godot with the -d flag, but it doesn't seem to change any output.

Computer 1:
CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D 16-Core
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 6800
OS: Arch Linux
Kernel: 6.18.0-3-cachyos
Mesa: 25.3.1
Vulkan Driver: vulkan-radeon 25.3.1
Desktop Environment: KDE Plasma 6.5.3 Wayland

- The crash occurs upon opening the scene with Occlusion Culling enabled, or by enabling Occlusion Culling while the scene is open
- The crash occurs regardless of the "Prefer Wayland" run setting
- The crash occurs both when the `--display-driver wayland` or `--display-driver x11` options are used
- The crash occurs both when the `--rendering-driver vulkan` or `--rendering-driver opengl` options are used
- Occasionally the editor does not crash when enabling occlusion culling, but it does crash more often than not.
- I **did not see** the error message that KellariKoodari noted above in my testing.

When the crash occurs, I see errors in dmesg stating there were general protection faults in libembree4.so.4 . I tried using every older version of Embree 4 on Arch to see if it was an issue with a later embree version, but the same crash occurred with every version.

- 4.0.1
- 4.1.0
- 4.2.0
- 4.3.0
- 4.3.1
- 4.3.2
- 4.3.3
- 4.4.0 (current)

Computer 2:
CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 7700X 8-Core
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT
OS: Arch Linux
Kernel: 6.17.9-arch
Mesa: 25.3.1
Vulkan Driver: vulkan-radeon 25.3.1
Desktop Environment: KDE Plasma 6.5.3 Wayland

- Basically the same exact behavior occured
- I did not test the older embree versions on this computer
- I **did see** the error message that KellariKoodari noted above one time
- I once get a backtrace from Godot

I'm attaching the Systemd journal logs for PC 1 and PC 2 when the crash occurred containing core dumps, and the Godot crash log from PC 2 when the crash occurred. These were all from the official arch godot package with `--display-driver wayland` and `--rendering-driver vulkan` set.

Please let me know if there's any more information I can provide or tests I can do that would help with identifying this. Thank you!

Edit: I tried making a dev build without the flags that the Arch package uses, and now it's not crashing. I had previously mirrored the Arch settings. I'll experiment with those flags and see if a particular one is causing the issue.

[pc1 - journal.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23997601/pc1.-.journal.log)
[pc2 - crash.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23997603/pc2.-.crash.log)
[pc2 - journal.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23997602/pc2.-.journal.log)

It's definitely related to embree somehow.

This build does not crash
```
scons dev_build=yes builtin_embree=yes
```

This build suffers from the crash
```
scons dev_build=yes builtin_embree=no
```

I tried building Godot 4.3 as KellariKoodari mentioned that the issue did not occur before 4.4. I was unable to build it on Arch due to compilation errors that I didn't know how to solve, so I built it inside of a Debian 13 container and then ran the compiled binary on my Arch host. The build built with `builtin_embree=yes` does not crash and the build built with `builtin_embree=no` crashes, just like 4.5.1 built on arch.

I've tested older embree 4 Arch packages with 4.5.1 as mentioned in my previous comment, and that did not change the behavior.

I tested an older version of onetbb, which is the one runtime dependency of embree other than gcc-libs and glibc, and the issue still occurred. The current version is 2022.3.0-2 and I tried 2022.0.0-1 which was the current version at the time 4.3 was built on Arch. I think if I were to try to downgrade gcc-libs or glibc it might break everything. Any other ideas of what I could try?

Hi, it seems like I am running into the same issue in the latest version. Any news ? I'd be happy to help by providing logs if it can be useful.

If it helps at all. I tried making a linux build with occlusion culling turned on and the built game had no crashing no matter how many times I tried it.

1. Turned on occlusion culling
2. Ran the game in editor, crash
3. Immediately made a build without changing anything and launched the build, no crash
4. Repeatedly closed and launched the build, no crash

@KellariKoodari What build command did you use specifically?

If you did not specify `builtin_embree=no`, then it defaults to `yes` and the issue doesn't occur. If you build it with `builtin_embree=no`, then the issue should occur which would be consistent with my findings.

@agsimmons Do you mean build command when building the Godot Editor itself from source or the game I build from the editor? If latter. Where do I edit the build command? 

To clarify. I did not build the editor itself, I just used the official Arch package and it crashes with Occlusion Culling, while a game built from the editor (Project -> Export) doesn't crash even with Occlusion Culling enabled.

@KellariKoodari Sorry I misunderstood and thought you built the editor. That's good to know that the built game itself runs; I haven't tried that yet.

I'm going to confirm that this still happens on 4.6-stable later.

@KellariKoodari have you tried baking the occluders or placing manually occluders/occludees with your setup ? So that the occlusion can actually happen. For reference, I followed [this guide](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/3d/occlusion_culling.html), going the automatic (and recommended) route.
For the record, I just updated to 4.6 (I wasn't aware it just released) and the issue seems to be gone on my side.
